cohort: 28 women with a history of previous cesarean section who had low lying as well as morbidly adherent placenta (MAP) of variable degree.
finding: Interval hysterectomy (delayed) resulted in significantly less estimated blood loss, volume of blood transfused, and shorter hospital stay compared to cesarean hysterectomy (immediate) in women with morbidly adherent placenta and previous cesarean sections.
followup_time: Duration of hospital stay (varied depending on the group)
